title: I Reached Out My Hand and Touched You...
text:
Your month of April slips down my neck...

Down my neck

your month of April slips

and its music tempers my misgiving.

By your hand the sky walks,

a friend,

and sets its gardens on my shoulders.

Your joy

unleashes your pack

of doves and archangels in heat,

and before the new

dawn I wake,

amid an ardent beating, from wing to wing.

Silver and

green you impose as your emblem

on hostile time, on exhausted waiting,

on the world already hurriedly recovered.

Who might possess the

portentous grace

of perpetuating the gift of your smile,

which turns my October into spring.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the April imagery, wing-beat movement, and the smile that turns October into spring.

title: Spellings of Harmony
text:
Spellings of harmony

tried by an inexperienced hand.

Tedium. Cacophony

of the everlasting piano

that I heard as a child

dreaming... I do not know of what,

of something that never came,

all that has already gone.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the child-memory of piano practice, boredom, and vanished expectation.

title: Advice
text:
I


This love that wants to be

perhaps soon will be;

but when shall return

what has just passed?

Today lies far from yesterday.

Yesterday is Nevermore!


II


A coin in the hand

perhaps should be kept:

the little coin of the soul

is lost if it is not given.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Machado's two aphoristic counsels on time and the soul's coin.

title: Traveler, There Is No Road
text:
Traveler, your footprints

are the road and nothing more;

Traveler, there is no road,

the road is made by walking.

By walking the road is made,

and turning one's gaze back

one sees the path that never

will be trodden again.

Traveler, there is no road

but wakes upon the sea.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the iconic road-made-by-walking image and the sea-wake ending.

title: Poetic Art
text:
And in the whole soul there is a single feast,

you will know it, Love, flowering shadow,

dream of aroma, and then... nothing; rags,

rancor, philosophy.

Broken in your mirror your finest idyll,

and already turned with your back to life,

your morning prayer must be:

Oh, beautiful day to be hanged!
editorial_note: The translation preserves the bitter collapse from love's feast into rags, rancor, and gallows-prayer.

title: Gloss
text:
Our lives are the rivers

that go to end in the sea,

which is dying. Great song!


Among my poets

Manrique has an altar.


Sweet joy of living:

bad science of passing,

blind flight to the sea.


Behind the terror of dying

is the pleasure of arriving.


Great pleasure!

But what of the horror of returning?

Great grief!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Machado's gloss on Manrique and the turn from arriving to returning.

title: Field
text:
The evening is dying

like a humble hearth going out.


There, over the mountains,

some embers remain.


And that broken tree on the white road

makes one weep with pity.


Two branches on the wounded trunk, and one

withered black leaf on each branch!


Are you crying?... Among the golden poplars,

far away, the shadow of love awaits you.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the dying-hearth sunset and the wounded tree before love's distant shadow.

title: Toward Lowland III
text:
An inn along my road.

With the gesture of a vestal,

you serve the red wine

of a suburban orgy.


The drunks

with lively eyes

and boastful tongues

pay you compliments, oh virago!


And other drunks sigh

for your diamond eyes,

your eyes that look at no one.


At the height of your breasts,

the overflowing tray

arrives in your brown arms.


Oh, woman,

give me also something to drink!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the tavern scene, vestal irony, and final request for drink.

title: Always Fugitive and Always...
text:
Always

fugitive and always

near me, in a black mantle,

poorly covered the

disdainful

gesture of your pale face.


I do not know where you go, nor where

your virgin beauty seeks a bed

in the night. I do not know

what dreams close your eyelids,

nor whose hand may have

half-opened

your inhospitable bed.

Stop your

step, elusive beauty,

stop your step.

I would like to kiss the bitter,

bitter flower of your lips.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the elusive black-mantled beauty and the bitter flower of the lips.
